saints.name: St. Bonaventure
saints.title: Bishop and Doctor of the Church
saints.shortBlurb: The “Seraphic Doctor,” Franciscan Minister General and cardinal, who wed learning to love and wrote the classic ascent of the soul to God…
biography: Born at Bagnoregio near Viterbo in 1221, Giovanni di Fidanza entered the Friars Minor and studied at Paris under Alexander of Hales, teaching theology there from 1248 until the secular masters' assault on the mendicant friars forced him to take up his pen in their defense. He received his doctorate together with Thomas Aquinas on 23 October 1257.

Elected Minister General on 2 February 1257, he governed for seventeen years a brotherhood torn between rigorists and the lax, steering a middle course that won him the name of the order's second founder. At the order's request he wrote the Legenda Major, the standard life of Saint Francis; his own mystical masterpiece, the Itinerarium Mentis in Deum, was composed on Mount La Verna in 1259.

Created Cardinal-Bishop of Albano by Gregory X in 1273, he guided the Second Council of Lyons toward the union with the Greeks proclaimed there on 6 July 1274, and died at Lyons nine days later, on 15 July, the council still in session. Canonized by Sixtus IV in 1482 and named Doctor of the Church by Sixtus V in 1588, he is venerated as the Seraphic Doctor.
saints.knownFor: Uniting rigorous theology with Franciscan mysticism; reforming and shaping the Friars Minor.

canonization.canonized: 1482 by Pope Sixtus IV; declared a Doctor of the Church in 1588 by Pope Sixtus V

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 14 July
